summary: Venus in Aries (Mesha), Mars' fire sign and neutral for Venus, gives passionate, impulsive and restless desire: strong attraction and adventurousness in love, with classical warnings about scandal, wasted money and unreliability, yet some capacity to lead groups.
common_outcomes: Strong, quick attractions and an adventurous approach to love
Restlessness; enjoys travel and the outdoors
Money spent freely on pleasure or influenced by flattery
Can be harsh or unreliable in commitments
rare_outcomes: Saravali 28.1-2: may rise to lead an army or a group of people
Saravali mentions risk of confinement or legal trouble connected with relationships
Brihat Jataka 18.14 (Venus in a Mars sign): disgrace to the family through affairs

by_area.personality: Saravali 28.1-2: hard in disposition and not reliable, yet eminent.
by_area.career: Saravali 28.1-2: may be an army chief or chief of men.
by_area.finance: Brihat Jataka 18.14 warns of losing wealth through others' flattery (Neely) or while pleading for women's faults (Sastri).
by_area.health: Saravali mentions weak night vision; do not convert into a medical claim.
by_area.relationships: The central area: classical texts warn of scandal and infidelity (Saravali 28.1-2; Brihat Jataka 18.14); loyalty and patience are growth areas.
by_area.family: Brihat Jataka warns of bringing disrepute on the family.

strengtheners: Saravali 28.25-30 (Aries/Scorpio group): Jupiter's aspect gives beautiful eyes, a charitable spouse, a handsome build and many children; Sun's aspect gives royal standing and learning despite losses through relationships
James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (navamsa section): a vargottama planet gives results like a planet in its own sign
weakeners_or_cancellations: Saravali 28.25-30: Moon's aspect gives fickleness, confinement, an unsuitable match and no children; Mars' aspect, loss of wealth, honour and happiness and menial work; Mercury's aspect, foolishness, profligacy and estrangement from relatives; Saturn's aspect, laziness, wandering and service to others
Sastri's note to Brihat Jataka 18.16: Venus is bad in the signs of malefics

James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (Sun and 'Combustion' sections): a planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and its significations and the houses it rules are spoiled

source_views.source: Saravali 28.1-2 (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Poor night vision, many faults, hostile, drawn to others' partners, wanders forests and hills, risk of confinement through relationships, harsh and unreliable, yet may lead an army or group.

source_views.source: Saravali 28.25-30, aspects on Venus in Aries/Scorpio (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Sun: losses and misery through women, yet royal standing and learning. Moon: confinement, fickle, unsuitable match, no children. Mars: without wealth, honour and happiness, menial work. Mercury: foolish, profligate, estranged, thievish. Jupiter: beautiful eyes, charitable spouse, handsome, many sons. Saturn: untidy, lazy, wandering, serves others.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.14 (tr. M. D. Neely)
source_views.view: Venus in a Mars sign: interest in others' spouses, loses wealth through flattery, brings disgrace on the family.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra ch. 3 (natural relationships)
source_views.view: Venus treats Mars as neutral, so Aries is a neutral sign.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.14 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed., p. 353)
source_views.view: Venus in a Mars sign: intrigues with others' wives, loses all wealth pleading on their behalf, a disgrace to the family. Sastri's note to 18.16: Venus is good for finance and material welfare in signs ruled by benefics and bad in signs of malefics and in its debilitation sign; it is good in Jupiter's signs; Venus in Makara or Kumbha may give handsomeness but not fortune.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer ('Sukra-Venus' section)
source_views.view: Mars and Jupiter are neutral to Venus.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (general rules: combustion, navamsa, house placements, dignities)
source_views.view: A planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and spoiled; a vargottama planet gives own-sign results, while a fallen planet that is vargottama is only worse off and a planet exalted in the birth chart but fallen in the navamsa gives very mixed results; a fallen planet is badly weakened unless well aspected; planets in kendras are powerful, in trikonas enhanced, in the 6th, 8th or 12th spoiled.

disagreements: Both texts are largely adverse about relationships. Saravali uniquely allows leadership of a group or army. The two Brihat Jataka translations differ on how wealth is lost (flattery in Neely, pleading for others in Sastri).
phrasing_guidance: Describe passionate, spontaneous affection and a need for excitement. Never predict infidelity or scandal; frame classical warnings as the value of patience and loyalty. Avoid medical claims about eyesight.

summary: Venus in Taurus (Vrishabha), its own earth sign, gives comfort, beauty, sensual refinement and prosperity: fine clothes, perfumes, land or livestock, generosity toward relatives and respected leadership. Malavya Yoga if in a kendra.
common_outcomes: Good looks, refined taste and enjoyment of comfort
Prosperity through land, agriculture, cattle, perfumes or fine goods
Generous; supports relatives
Learned in many fields and respected
rare_outcomes: Saravali 28.3-4: many partners and jewels (read as a rich social and romantic life)
Brihat Jataka 18.14 (own sign): wealth through own strength and intelligence, honoured by rulers, community leader, famous and fearless
Malavya Mahapurusha Yoga in a kendra (Phaladeepika 6.1, 6.3)

by_area.personality: Saravali 28.3-4: charitable, helps living beings, good appearance.

by_area.finance: Brihat Jataka 18.14: money by own exertion and intelligence. Saravali: gems, perfumes, garlands and fine clothes.
by_area.relationships: Saravali's 'many wives' is a period marker of wealth; Raman (Malavya) promises happiness from spouse and children when the yoga forms.
by_area.spirituality: Raman (Malavya Yoga remarks): Malavya inclines to pleasure, with spiritual advancement in inverse ratio to comforts.

James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (navamsa section): a vargottama planet gives results like a planet in its own sign

James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (Sun and 'Combustion' sections): a planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and its significations and the houses it rules are spoiled

Raman's table (Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 20) places it in the 1st for Taurus lagna, the 7th for Scorpio, the 10th for Leo and the 4th for Aquarius; he adds that unblemished Malavya is exceptional.

source_views.view: Venus in a kendra in its own or exaltation sign: well-developed physique, strong-minded, wealthy, happy with spouse and children, vehicles, clean senses, renowned and learned. It inclines to pleasure and a materialistic outlook, spiritual advancement being in inverse ratio to comforts. Lagna table: Taurus, Libra, Pisces lagnas in the 1st; Aries, Scorpio, Virgo in the 7th; Gemini, Leo, Capricorn in the 10th; Sagittarius, Aquarius, Cancer in the 4th. Unblemished cases are exceptional.

source_views.view: Exalted Venus is not about being a great artist, as it can be when Venus is in its own sign, nor about wealth.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer ('Sukra-Venus' section)
source_views.view: Venus owns Taurus and Libra and gives very good results in those signs.

phrasing_guidance: Describe comfort, beauty and steady prosperity as supported tendencies. Do not suggest multiple marriages; Saravali's line reflects its era.

Skilled in writing, poetry or performing arts
Earns through music, dance or creative work
Many friends; loyal in friendship

Saravali 28.5-6: known for learning and scripture; honours the learned

summary: Venus in Cancer (Karka), the Moon's water sign and an enemy's sign for Venus, gives emotional, gentle and nurturing affection with comfort and good character, but classical texts warn of emotional turbulence, indulgence and recurring domestic difficulties.
common_outcomes: Gentle, wise, virtuous and good-looking
Gets the comforts desired
Strong emotional needs in relationships
Recurring family or domestic difficulties
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka 18.16: two marriages, timidity and sorrow through desire
Saravali mentions trouble through relationships and drink

by_area.finance: Saravali: desired happiness and wealth. Brihat Jataka 18.16 (Sastri): seeks monetary help from others.
by_area.relationships: Classical texts warn of turbulence: troubles through women (Saravali) and, in Brihat Jataka, two marriages.

Loved by relatives; helps others
Respectful toward teachers and elders
Some dissatisfaction despite comforts
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka 18.16: a distinguished young spouse and few children
Saravali mentions reduced vigour and lack of fine judgement

summary: Venus in Virgo (Kanya) is debilitated, deepest at 27 degrees: pleasure, romance and aesthetic ease are filtered through analysis and criticism. Classical texts describe a gentle, skilled, helpful person with modest or service-oriented work and mixed relationship results; neecha bhanga is frequent.
common_outcomes: Gentle, skilled, helpful and sweet-spoken (Saravali)
Love shown through service and practical care (astromedha)
Earnings from several sources (Saravali)
Exacting standards in relationships (astromedha)

Brihat Jataka 18.15: very lowly work (Neely) or base acts (Sastri)
With cancellation, powerful results (Foss)

by_area.finance: Saravali: earns money through several sources.
by_area.relationships: Saravali 28.11-12: low company, little happiness and pleasure. Braha: Venus in Virgo often brings overindulgence in sensual pleasures. Foss: desire may be held back by a search for purity. astromedha: risk of over-criticising partners.
by_area.spirituality: Pilgrimage and practical devotion (Saravali). Foss: Virgo seeks the sacred and the pure within the impure.

Raman (no. 250) reads the cancelling planet as the one exalted in Virgo, i.e. Mercury, in a kendra from the lagna or Moon
Foss: Venus in Virgo is not defiled and can give powerful results if well placed, certainly if with Mercury or if Mercury or Jupiter is strongly placed in an angle

Saravali 28.37-42 (Gemini/Virgo group): Sun's aspect gives favour from authority and wealth; Moon's aspect gives beauty and luck; Mercury's aspect gives learning, wealth and leadership; Jupiter's aspect gives happiness and a teaching role

Deepest debility at 27 degrees Virgo (BPHS 3.50)
James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (navamsa section): a debilitated planet that is also vargottama is only worse off

source_views.view: Venus in Virgo: the person will do base acts.

source_views.view: The lord of the debilitation sign, or the planet exalted there, in a kendra from the lagna or Moon cancels debility. Raman reads 'thaduchchanatha' as the planet exalted in that sign (Mercury, for Venus in Virgo) and notes the reading is disputed.

source_views.source: Andrew Foss, The Yoga of the Planets: Venus, Shukra, name 2
source_views.view: Venus is debilitated in Virgo, whose agenda is to seek the sacred and the pure within the impure; desire may be rejected as unsuited to that quest, so Venus can seem weak, but it is not defiled and can give powerful results if well placed, certainly if with Mercury or if Mercury or Jupiter is strong in an angle.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer ('Sukra-Venus' section)
source_views.view: Venus operates worst in Virgo, its fallen sign; in Virgo it often brings overindulgence in sex or sensual pleasures.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (general rules: combustion, navamsa, house placements, dignities)
source_views.view: A planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and spoiled; a vargottama planet gives own-sign results, while a fallen planet that is vargottama is only worse off and a planet exalted in the birth chart but fallen in the navamsa gives very mixed results; a fallen planet is badly weakened unless well aspected; planets in kendras are powerful, in trikonas enhanced, in the 6th, 8th or 12th spoiled.

disagreements: Saravali's verse is mixed (gentle and skilled but stingy); Brihat Jataka gives only a terse negative line. Modern authors read the debility in opposite ways: Braha says Virgo Venus tends to overindulgence, while Foss and astromedha describe desire held back by purity or criticism. On cancellation, Phaladeepika uses kendra placement from lagna/Moon or aspect; Foss names Mercury conjunct Venus. BPHS and Braha make Mercury and Venus mutual friends.
phrasing_guidance: Never say the person will be unhappy in love or do menial work. Describe a caring, practical and discerning way of loving, and suggest self-acceptance and balance as growth areas. Always check neecha bhanga before giving a weak reading.

Brave and capable in duties; protects own people
Fond of travel or living in other places
